edges.note: Motivos formalmente parecidos; no se afirma identidad doctrinal ni transmisión histórica directa.
Emparejamiento o pares de almas no equivalen al origen white-fire/twin-flame.
Un emparejamiento previo no implica cláusulas de aprendizaje o acuerdo bilateral.
Elegir pruebas antes de nacer hace inteligible un plan previo, pero no demuestra contrato entre dos almas.
No usar Mónada como sinónimo automático de pareja monádica o twin flame.
Aporta un marco alma-personalidad-propósito, no la gramática contractual de ALMAS.
La utilización de la dracónica como capa contractual es una operacionalización ALMAS, no doctrina de Crane.
La experiencia reportada no discrimina origen metafísico.
Kardec explicitly situates choice before incarnation at the level of the type of trial, not every detail.
Kardec treats chosen trials and requested missions in distinct passages; ALMAS must not collapse them.
Choice of general trials coexists with freedom in contingent actions and outcomes.
A chosen type of trial does not establish that another specific soul contracted to provide it.
A requested mission can be individual or collective and does not by itself establish a dyadic soul contract.
Regression/interlife literature is a major modern vehicle for reported pre-birth planning.
A soul plan may include relationships, but a bilateral contract is a more specific hypothesis.
Myss's sacred contract concerns personal purpose and archetypal structure; it is not automatically a bilateral preincarnational pact.
Continuity across lives can explain relational significance without requiring a consciously planned bilateral contract.
Membership in a soul-group model does not establish a specific contract between two members.
Even under a contract hypothesis, outcomes remain contingent; contract function and encarnated result must be separated.
Sotah 2a supplies an early rabbinic first/second-match framework later reworked in kabbalistic contexts.
Zoharic paired-soul imagery supplies a strong doctrinal context for later discussion of pairing.
Zivug is a Jewish/kabbalistic relational category; it does not entail the modern white-fire-ovoid twin-flame doctrine.
A true/corresponding mate in Lurianic language is not doctrinally identical to modern twin flame.
Reincarnational continuity can explain recurrence without implying a consciously planned bilateral agreement.
Rectification can describe function or purpose without establishing that two souls contracted the relationship beforehand.
Both can involve purpose or repair, but derive from different doctrinal systems and cannot be collapsed.
Lurianic soul-root structures and Theosophical Monad terminology belong to distinct ontologies.
Both can describe supra-individual relatedness, but their genealogies and structures differ.
A shared or related root can involve networks of souls and does not imply a unique romantic counterpart.
Lurianic networks of soul-root relations weaken any automatic inference from related roots to an exclusive dyadic origin.
First/second zivug terminology is not a stage model of twin-flame relationships.
A corresponding mate does not by itself establish negotiated preincarnational clauses.
The phrase predates Summit Lighthouse in Victorian esoteric fiction; later doctrinal codification must be treated separately.
Corelli's half-flame imagery resembles later counterpart models but does not establish direct doctrinal continuity.
Twin soul and twin flame circulate in adjacent Victorian esoteric-literary contexts but are not assumed identical.
Theosophist reception documents circulation of twin-flame language without establishing doctrinal endorsement.
Blavatsky's Monad belongs to Theosophical cosmology and is not a romantic dyad.
Theosophical Monad and Lurianic soul-root are distinct ontological structures.
Division/reunion motifs are comparable but do not establish direct transmission or doctrinal identity.
Bailey supplies an esoteric soul-development framework, not a dyadic contract-extraction technique.
Bailey's monad-soul-personality distinctions do not by themselves define a twin-flame pair.
Soul/personality is an intrapersonal ontological relation, not masculine/feminine pair polarity.
Individual evolutionary-stage interpretation is distinct from phenomenology of a relationship.
ALMAS's use of draconic recurrence in contract analysis is a project operationalization, not Crane's doctrine.
A nodal transformation technique does not establish reincarnation.
Instant recognition can occur in relationships participants call soulmate/twin flame but does not establish origin.
Reported synchronicity may inform lived meaning or chronology but does not prove a pre-birth agreement.
Transformation is compatible with karmic/evolutionary interpretations but is not specific enough to diagnose them.
Transformative impact appears across multiple relationship forms and cannot discriminate twin-flame origin.
A participant or community label is D_CONTEMPORARY_USAGE, not C_DOCTRINE or ontological validation.
Soul-contract theodicy shares pre-birth planning themes but should not be presented as Kardec's doctrine.
ALMAS may study contemporary soul-contract vocabulary but its astrological reconstruction is independently defined.
New Age scholarship contextualizes modern esoteric synthesis but does not validate a specific doctrine.
